title: Impact of Crop Insurance Subsidy Reform on Agricultural Land Use

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with unit and period fixed effects (two-way fixed effects).
- Why: We observe treated and control farms before and after the subsidy reform. The DID interaction treated × post identifies the causal effect of more favorable insurance terms on log acres planted.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the reform, treated and control farms would have experienced the same average change in log acres over time.
  - No differential composition or anticipation effects: Treatment status is fixed and the reform was not anticipated in a way that differentially affected treated units’ pre-trends.
  - Stable treatment timing and SUTVA: No spillovers from treated to control farms.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(fixest)
})

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s40_data.csv"
dt <- fread(path)

# Basic checks
dt <- dt[!is.na(y) & !is.na(treated) & !is.na(post)]
dt[, unit_id := as.factor(unit_id)]
# Keep period numeric for trends/event-study; also make a labeled factor for FE
# (fixest handles numeric FE fine)
n_units <- uniqueN(dt$unit_id)
n_periods <- uniqueN(dt$period)

cat("Sample size:", nrow(dt), " | Units:", n_units, " | Periods:", n_periods, "\n")

# 2) Main DID: y ~ treated:post | unit FE + time FE; cluster at unit level
est_main <- feols(y ~ treated:post | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id)

b <- coef(est_main)[["treated:post"]]
se <- se(est_main)[["treated:post"]]
p <- pvalue(est_main)[["treated:post"]]
zcrit <- qnorm(0.975)
ci_lo <- b - zcrit * se
ci_hi <- b + zcrit * se

# Transform to percent change
pct <- 100 * (exp(b) - 1)
pct_lo <- 100 * (exp(ci_lo) - 1)
pct_hi <- 100 * (exp(ci_hi) - 1)

cat("\nMAIN DID RESULT (unit and period FE, clustered by unit):\n")
cat(sprintf("Log-point effect = %.4f (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f)\n", b, se, p))
cat(sprintf("Percent effect = %.2f%%  (95%% CI: %.2f%%, %.2f%%)\n", pct, pct_lo, pct_hi))

# 3) Simple difference-in-means DID (sanity check, no FE)
avg <- dt[, .(mean_y = mean(y)), by = .(treated, post)]
m_tp <- avg[treated == 1 & post == 1, mean_y]
m_t0 <- avg[treated == 1 & post == 0, mean_y]
m_cp <- avg[treated == 0 & post == 1, mean_y]
m_c0 <- avg[treated == 0 & post == 0, mean_y]
did_simple <- (m_tp - m_t0) - (m_cp - m_c0)
cat("\nSIMPLE DID (difference-in-means, on log y):\n")
cat(sprintf("Log-point DID = %.4f  | Percent = %.2f%%\n", did_simple, 100 * (exp(did_simple) - 1)))

# 4) Robustness: Two-way clustering (unit and period)
est_twoc <- feols(y ~ treated:post | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id + period)
b2 <- coef(est_twoc)[["treated:post"]]
se2 <- se(est_twoc)[["treated:post"]]
p2 <- pvalue(est_twoc)[["treated:post"]]
pct2 <- 100 * (exp(b2) - 1)
cat("\nROBUSTNESS: Two-way clustered SE (unit and period):\n")
cat(sprintf("Log-point = %.4f (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f) | Percent = %.2f%%\n", b2, se2, p2, pct2))

# 5) Robustness: Unit-specific linear trends (if 3+ periods)
if (n_periods >= 3) {
  est_trend <- feols(y ~ treated:post | unit_id + period + unit_id^period, data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id)
  bT <- coef(est_trend)[["treated:post"]]
  seT <- se(est_trend)[["treated:post"]]
  pT <- pvalue(est_trend)[["treated:post"]]
  pctT <- 100 * (exp(bT) - 1)
  cat("\nROBUSTNESS: Adding unit-specific linear trends:\n")
  cat(sprintf("Log-point = %.4f (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f) | Percent = %.2f%%\n", bT, seT, pT, pctT))
} else {
  cat("\nROBUSTNESS: Unit-specific trends skipped (need >= 3 periods).\n")
}

# 6) Robustness: Event-study pre-trend check (if multiple pre-periods exist)
pre_periods <- sort(unique(dt[post == 0, period]))
post_periods <- sort(unique(dt[post == 1, period]))
if (length(pre_periods) >= 2 && length(post_periods) >= 1) {
  base_period <- max(pre_periods)
  est_es <- feols(y ~ i(period, treated, ref = base_period) | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id)
  cat("\nEVENT STUDY (baseline =", base_period, "): selected coefficients (pre-periods should be ~0):\n", sep = " ")
  coefs_es <- coef(est_es)
  nm_es <- names(coefs_es)
  # Extract pre-period coefficients
  pre_names <- nm_es[grepl("^period::\\d+#treated$", nm_es)]
  pre_names <- pre_names[sapply(strsplit(pre_names, "::|#"), function(v) as.numeric(v[2]) < base_period)]
  if (length(pre_names) > 0) {
    for (nm in pre_names) {
      cat(sprintf("  %s = %.4f\n", nm, coefs_es[[nm]]))
    }
  } else {
    cat("  No multiple pre-periods to display.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("\nEVENT STUDY: skipped (need >=2 pre-periods and >=1 post-period).\n")
}

# 7) Robustness: Placebo DID on pre-periods only (fake reform at last pre-period)
if (length(pre_periods) >= 2) {
  last_pre <- max(pre_periods)
  dt_pre <- dt[post == 0]
  dt_pre[, placebo_post := as.integer(period >= last_pre)]
  est_placebo <- feols(y ~ treated:placebo_post | unit_id + period, data = dt_pre, cluster = ~ unit_id)
  bP <- coef(est_placebo)[["treated:placebo_post"]]
  seP <- se(est_placebo)[["treated:placebo_post"]]
  pP <- pvalue(est_placebo)[["treated:placebo_post"]]
  cat("\nPLACEBO (pre-periods only; fake reform at last pre-period):\n")
  cat(sprintf("Log-point = %.4f (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f)\n", bP, seP, pP))
} else {
  cat("\nPLACEBO: skipped (need >= 2 pre-periods).\n")
}

# 8) Robustness: Trim extreme outcome values (1% tails) and re-estimate
qs <- quantile(dt$y, probs = c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)
dt_trim <- dt[y >= qs[1] & y <= qs[2]]
est_trim <- feols(y ~ treated:post | unit_id + period, data = dt_trim, cluster = ~ unit_id)
b_trim <- coef(est_trim)[["treated:post"]]
se_trim <- se(est_trim)[["treated:post"]]
p_trim <- pvalue(est_trim)[["treated:post"]]
pct_trim <- 100 * (exp(b_trim) - 1)
cat("\nROBUSTNESS: Trim 1% tails of y:\n")
cat(sprintf("Log-point = %.4f (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f) | Percent = %.2f%%  (N = %d)\n",
            b_trim, se_trim, p_trim, pct_trim, nrow(dt_trim)))

# Final clear numerical result (main estimate)
cat("\n=== SUMMARY: Estimated percent change in acres planted due to subsidy reform ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Main DID (unit & period FE, unit-clustered SE): %.2f%% (95%% CI: %.2f%%, %.2f%%)\n",
            pct, pct_lo, pct_hi))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. More favorable insurance reduces downside risk and typically encourages input use and land allocation to insured crops, so farmers expand planted acreage.
- Magnitude: A modest increase, approximately 3–8% in acres planted (in logs). The effect is larger where risk exposure is higher or credit constraints bind, and smaller where farmers were already well insured or face binding land constraints.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log acres planted between treated and untreated farms before and after the subsidy reform.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The subsidy reform led to an increase in the log of acres planted.
